reason: The light-sensitive cells and relay cells are complementary parts of the retina.
expectation: They will form a retinal network that detects light and passes signals onward.

effect: The retinas now link light-sensitive cells to nerve fibers; they need to be incorporated into the eyes.
reaction: The relay from sensors to nerve fibers is a useful connection.
reason: The eye walls provide the structure in which to place the retinas.
expectation: The retinas will line the inside of the eye walls.

effect: The retinas now line eye cups with three named front-fitting slots.
reaction: The slots make the next construction steps clear.
reason: The transparent corneas match the clear-front slots.
expectation: The corneas will fit into the clear fronts of the eye cups.

effect: The corneas fill the clear-front slots and bend incoming light.
reaction: The light-ray inset clarifies their focusing role.
reason: The lenses match the focusing-lens slots in the eye cups.
expectation: The lenses will fit behind the corneas to help focus light.

effect: The lenses are fitted; their shape changes how much they bend light. The light-control slots remain.
reaction: The comparison makes the lenses' flexible focusing role clearer.
reason: The irises surround the pupils and match the remaining light-control slots.
expectation: The irises will fit into the eye cups to control the light entering each eye.

effect: The eye cups now have all three fittings, with light focused onto the retinas; they still need brain connections and movement.
reaction: The ray diagram usefully distinguishes focusing from controlling light entry.
reason: The visual pathways should connect the completed eye structures to the brain.
expectation: The optic nerves and visual pathways will connect to the retinas.

effect: The eyes now connect through optic nerves toward brain relays; the outgoing signals are neural, not light.
reaction: The contrast between incoming light and outgoing nerve signals is useful.
reason: The eye-moving muscles and nerves should add the movement required by the goal.

effect: The eyes now have opposing muscles and motor nerves; they still need to be integrated with the body.

reason: The remaining body and equipped eyes should join to complete the goal.

choice.with: Eyes with pathways and moving muscles

expectation: The eyes and their visual and motor pathways will connect to the body's existing brain.

reaction: The face-looking example gives the assembled parts a clear purpose.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the irises and seeing the complete ray diagram was most worthwhile: the planned illustration distinguishes focusing light from controlling how much enters.

leastWorthwhile.text: The separate fitting steps were straightforward and somewhat repetitive, though the cornea and lens insets gave them distinct educational purposes.

surprise.text: The contrast between light entering the eye and nerve signals leaving it sharpened my understanding of what the visual pathway carries.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; the named slots made the fittings predictable rather than arbitrary.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the constructions linked physical parts to their functions, although I would hope for more meaningful choices than the largely obvious fittings here.
